theme: Moral crisis, emotional overwhelm, and paralysis in the face of duty
summary: Arjuna observes his kinsmen, teachers, and loved ones assembled on Kurukshetra. Overwhelmed by grief, compassion, and confusion, his bow Gandiva slips from his trembling hand, and he refuses to fight.

keyVerses.speaker: Arjuna
keyVerses.transliteration: dṛṣṭvemaṁ svajanaṁ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṁ samupasthitam | sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṁ ca pariśuṣyati || vepathuś ca śarīre me roma-harṣaś ca jāyate | gāṇḍīvaṁ sraṁsate hastāt tvak caiva paridahyate ||
keyVerses.translation: O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen gathered here eager to battle, my limbs fail and my mouth becomes dry. My body trembles, my hair stands on end, my bow Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns all over.
keyVerses.context: Arjuna experiences visceral psychosomatic collapse because his love for his family conflicts with his duty as a Kshatriya warrior defending righteousness.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: When a person feels physically and emotionally paralyzed by difficult life choices, Arjuna's vulnerability proves that even the greatest warriors experience moments where emotion overcomes the intellect.

englishTitle: The Yoga of Knowledge and Discernment
theme: The eternal soul, equanimity, detachment from fruits of action, and the steady intellect (Sthitaprajna)
summary: Krishna begins his divine instruction. He reveals the imperishable nature of the soul (Atman), introduces Karma Yoga—the science of selfless action without attachment to outcomes—and describes the qualities of one whose intellect is completely steady.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ | āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata ||
keyVerses.translation: O son of Kunti, the contact between the senses and sense objects gives rise to fleeting sensations of heat and cold, pleasure and pain. They come and go and are impermanent; learn to endure them patiently, O Bharata.
keyVerses.context: Krishna instructs Arjuna that dualities like joy and sorrow are natural sensations arising from external circumstances, but they should not destabilize the core of one's consciousness.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Vital for anyone suffering heartbreak, disappointment, or sudden adversity. Reminder that the emotional storm is temporary and does not define their permanent self.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṁ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
keyVerses.translation: The soul is never born, nor does it ever die; nor having once been, does it ever cease to be. It is unborn, eternal, ever-existing, undying and primeval. It is not slain when the body is slain.
keyVerses.context: Krishna addresses Arjuna's existential fear of causing death and loss by highlighting that the essential self is indestructible.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Provides deep comfort to those grieving the loss of loved ones or mourning endings in their lives.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stvakarmaṇi ||
keyVerses.translation: You have a right only to perform your prescribed duty, but never to the fruits of your actions. Let not the fruit of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
keyVerses.context: The seminal verse on Nishkama Karma (selfless action). Krishna frees Arjuna from the anxiety of victory or defeat by anchoring focus purely on present effort.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Essential for exam anxiety, career pressure, fear of failure, and overthinking future outcomes.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: dhyāyato viṣayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate | saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate || krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ | smṛti-bhraṁśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati ||
keyVerses.translation: While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment to them; from attachment arises desire, and from unfulfilled desire arises anger. From anger arises delusion; from delusion comes loss of memory; from loss of memory comes ruin of the intellect; and when the intellect is ruined, a person is destroyed.
keyVerses.context: Krishna traces the psychological ladder of ruin, demonstrating how subtle fixation degrades into blind wrath and loss of discernment.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Crucial for users struggling with rage, obsession, jealousy, or impulses of revenge.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṁś carati niḥspṛhaḥ | nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati ||
keyVerses.translation: That person who has given up all desires for sense gratification, who lives free from longing, who has eliminated the sense of false ownership ('mine') and false ego ('I'), attains true peace.
keyVerses.context: Krishna defines the state of true, unshakable peace (Shanti).
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Healing from breakup, possessiveness, or wounded pride.

theme: Action as sacrifice, setting an example for society, conquering lust and selfish desire
summary: Arjuna asks why he should engage in violent warfare if knowledge is superior. Krishna explains that no one can remain actionless even for a moment. Proper action performed as an offering (Yajna) and for the welfare of the world (Lokasamgraha) purifies the mind.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ | sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate ||
keyVerses.translation: Whatever actions a great person performs, common people follow. Whatever standards they set by exemplary acts, all the world pursues.
keyVerses.context: Krishna urges leaders and mentors to act with highest integrity because their conduct sets the moral tone for others.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Guidance on leadership, parenting, elder sibling duty, and professional role modeling.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣṭhitāt | sva-dharme nidhanaṁ śreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
keyVerses.translation: It is far better to perform one's own natural duty (Sva-dharma), even if imperfectly, than to attempt another's duty skillfully. Death in the performance of one's own duty is auspicious; pursuing another's path is fraught with peril.
keyVerses.context: Krishna advises against imitating others' paths out of vanity or social pressure.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Directly resolves career dilemmas, imposter syndrome, and the trap of social comparison.

englishTitle: The Yoga of Knowledge and the Renunciation of Action
theme: The descent of the Divine, the fire of wisdom consuming karma, resolving doubts
summary: Krishna reveals his eternal presence across ages, explaining the purpose of his incarnation (Avatar) to protect the good and establish dharma. He teaches that doubts are resolved through spiritual knowledge.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata | abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham || paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
keyVerses.translation: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in righteousness, O descendant of Bharata, and an increase in unrighteousness, at that time I manifest Myself. For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil, and for the re-establishment of righteousness, I appear age after age.
keyVerses.context: The cosmic assurance that righteousness is ultimately safeguarded.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Offers reassurance in times of despair, cynicism about the world, or feelings of systemic injustice.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṁ pavitram iha vidyate | tat svayaṁ yoga-saṁsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati ||
keyVerses.translation: In this world, there is nothing as purifying as transcendental knowledge. One who has attained perfection in yoga finds this knowledge within their own heart in due course of time.
keyVerses.context: Wisdom is described as the supreme purifier of the mind and doubts.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Encourages study, self-reflection, and patience when seeking clarity.

theme: True renunciation is inner freedom, not physical abandonment of responsibilities
summary: Krishna harmonizes the path of monastic renunciation and active selfless work. The lotus leaf sits in water yet remains untouched by drops; similarly, one who acts dedicating results to the divine remains untainted by sin.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ | lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā ||
keyVerses.translation: One who performs duties without attachment, surrendering the results unto the Supreme, is not affected by sinful reactions, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
keyVerses.context: Illustrates how to live fully engaged in society without becoming stained by toxicity or attachment.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Helps users maintain boundaries in stressful work environments or toxic relationships.

englishTitle: The Yoga of Meditation and Self-Control
theme: Mastering the restless mind, meditation, the mind as friend or enemy, overcoming failure in spiritual pursuit
summary: Krishna describes the practice of meditation, posture, moderation in food and sleep, and the discipline of thoughts. When Arjuna laments that the mind is as impossible to control as the fierce wind, Krishna reassures him that it is mastered through practice (Abhyasa) and dispassion (Vairagya).

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet | ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ || bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatru-vat ||
keyVerses.translation: Let a person lift themselves by their own mind, and not degrade themselves. For the mind is the greatest friend of the self, and the mind is also the greatest enemy of the self. For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best friend; but for one who has failed to do so, the mind remains an enemy like an external foe.
keyVerses.context: Krishna places the responsibility for elevation and degradation squarely upon the individual's inner relationship with their mind.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Pivotal for users battling depression, self-loathing, procrastination, or negative self-talk.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna & Arjuna
keyVerses.transliteration: cañcalaṁ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham | tasyāhaṁ nigrahaṁ manye vāyor iva su-duṣkaram || asaṁśayaṁ mahā-bāho mano durnigrahaṁ calam | abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate ||
keyVerses.translation: Arjuna: 'The mind is restless, turbulent, obstinate and very strong, O Krishna. To curb it, I think, is harder than controlling the wind.' Krishna: 'Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and difficult to curb. But by sustained practice (Abhyāsa) and detachment (Vairāgya), it can be restrained.'
keyVerses.context: Krishna does not dismiss Arjuna's frustration; he validates that the mind is indeed difficult, but provides the twin cures of patience and steady practice.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Validation for anyone struggling to build habits, focus, or quiet racing thoughts.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśas tasya vidyate | na hi kalyāṇa-kṛt kaścid durgatiṁ tāta gacchati ||
keyVerses.translation: O Parth, neither in this world nor in the next is there destruction for one who strives for goodness. One who does good, My dear friend, never treads the path of ruin.
keyVerses.context: Krishna reassures Arjuna that sincere effort on the noble path is never wasted, even if one dies or stumbles halfway.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Massive reassurance for users devastated by failure after genuine hard work.

englishTitle: The Yoga of Knowledge and Realization
theme: The divine nature behind creation, the four types of seekers, transcending Maya
summary: Krishna describes his material and spiritual energies. He mentions the four kinds of pious people who turn to the divine: the distressed, the seeker of wealth, the seeker of knowledge, and the wise person who knows the divine truth.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: catur-vidhā bhajante māṁ janāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna | ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha ||
keyVerses.translation: Four kinds of virtuous people turn to Me with devotion, O Arjuna: the distressed (ārtaḥ), the seeker of truth (jijñāsuḥ), the seeker of material prosperity (arthārthī), and the person of wisdom (jñānī).
keyVerses.context: Shows that coming to the divine or higher wisdom out of distress or sorrow is natural and fully accepted.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Removes shame for turning to spiritual guidance only during grief or crisis.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Imperishable Absolute
theme: Transcendence of death, continuous remembrance of truth, and attainment of the eternal realm
summary: Arjuna asks about Brahman, the self, action, and how one can attain steady remembrance at the time of departing this physical body. Krishna explains that what one meditates upon with devotion throughout life shapes one's ultimate consciousness and destination.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: yaṁ yaṁ vāpi smaran bhāvaṁ tyajaty ante kalevaram | taṁ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ ||
keyVerses.translation: Whatever state of being one remembers when leaving the body at death, that state alone one attains, O son of Kunti, having constantly contemplated it during one's lifetime.
keyVerses.context: Krishna instructs that one's final state of consciousness is not an accidental miracle, but the natural culmination of one's daily thoughts and inner practices.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Crucial for guiding users struggling with anxiety about their future or mortality, emphasizing that current mindfulness and consistent inner discipline shape their ultimate destiny.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Sovereign Science and Sovereign Secret
theme: Unconditional grace, the simplicity of devotion, redemption of all souls
summary: Krishna discloses the royal secret of divine love and presence. Even the simplest leaf, flower, fruit, or water offered with love is accepted. No one is inherently barred from redemption.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: ananyāś cintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham ||
keyVerses.translation: To those who always remember Me with undivided devotion, meditating upon My form, I personally carry what they lack and preserve what they already possess (Yoga-Kṣema).
keyVerses.context: The divine pledge of spiritual and material stewardship for those who surrender their burdens.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Instills profound trust for users experiencing overwhelming loneliness and fear of abandonment.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati | tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ ||
keyVerses.translation: Whoever offers Me with love and devotion a simple leaf, a flower, a fruit, or even a drop of water—that offering, given from a pure heart, I accept with joy.
keyVerses.context: Rejects elaborate wealth or ritualistic pretension in favor of sincere inner intention.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Encourages users feeling inadequate that small, genuine steps matter more than grand demonstrations.

englishTitle: The Yoga of Divine Glories and Manifestations
theme: The omnipresence of the divine in all excellence, power, truth, and creation
summary: Krishna describes how all grandeur, beauty, brilliance, and excellence in the universe originates as a spark of the supreme consciousness. He identifies himself with the pinnacle of every category: among mountains, Meru; among senses, the mind; among warriors, Rama.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ śrīmad ūrjitam eva vā | tat tad evāvagaccha tvaṁ mama tejo-'ṁśa-sambhavam ||
keyVerses.translation: Whatever creation is opulent, beautiful, or glorious, understand that it springs from but a single spark of My splendor.
keyVerses.context: Krishna invites Arjuna to cultivate reverence for all magnificent achievements and natural splendor in the cosmos.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Assists users suffering from cynicism, loss of wonder, or nihilism by reorienting perception toward appreciation and gratitude.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Vision of the Cosmic Form
theme: The revelation of universal reality, the awe-inspiring and terrifying nature of Time (Kala)
summary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals his cosmic form containing all galaxies, gods, suns, and the inexorable march of Time consuming all warriors. Arjuna is awe-struck and terrified, recognizing the immense scope of reality beyond his tiny human vantage point.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: kālo 'smi loka-kṣaya-kṛt pravṛddho lokān samāhartum iha pravṛttaḥ... tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṁ samṛddham | mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savya-sācin ||
keyVerses.translation: I am Time, the great destroyer of worlds, having grown mighty to annihilate these realms... Therefore, arise! Attain glory, conquer your adversaries, and enjoy a prosperous kingdom. By Me these warriors have already been slain; you be merely an instrument (Nimitta-mātra), O ambidextrous archer!
keyVerses.context: Krishna reveals that the grand currents of destiny and consequence are already in motion; Arjuna is called not to carry the burden of the universe, but simply to fulfill his duty courageously.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Inspires courage in those burdened by the feeling that the entire weight of a company, family, or situation rests solely upon their shoulders.

theme: The qualities of the beloved companion of the divine: compassion, absence of malice, equanimity
summary: Arjuna asks whether it is better to meditate on the formless unmanifest or on the personal divine. Krishna praises devotion and enumerates the traits of someone truly dear to him: free from jealousy, friendly to all, patient, forgiving, and unaffected by praise or blame.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca | nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣamī || santuṣṭaḥ satataṁ yogī yatātmā dṛḍha-niścayaḥ | mayy arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||
keyVerses.translation: One who bears no malice toward any living being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and egotism, tranquil in sorrow and joy, forgiving, ever content, steady in meditation, self-restrained and firm in conviction, with mind and intellect surrendered unto Me—such a person is dear to Me.
keyVerses.context: Portrait of the ideal human character: gentleness paired with emotional stability.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Guidance on overcoming resentment, forgiving past abusers/partners, and cultivating quiet strength.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Field and the Knower of the Field
theme: Discrimination between the physical body/psyche (the field) and the witnessing consciousness (the knower)
summary: Krishna distinguishes between the Kṣetra (the physical-mental instrument: senses, emotions, desires, thoughts) and the Kṣetrajña (the witness consciousness that observes them without being stained by them).

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: idaṁ śarīraṁ kaunteya kṣetram ity abhidhīyate | etad yo vetti taṁ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tad-vidaḥ ||
keyVerses.translation: This body, O son of Kunti, is called the field (Kṣetra); and whoever observes and knows it is proclaimed by the wise to be the knower of the field (Kṣetrajña).
keyVerses.context: Krishna introduces the foundational cognitive reframing of Vedanta: you are not your emotions, thoughts, or physical symptoms; you are the awareness that observes them.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Profound tool for anxiety, panic, and heartbreak: helps users step back from overwhelming emotions by recognizing that their core observer self is unharmed.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Three Modes of Nature
theme: The three psychological forces (Sattva, Rajas, Tamas) and how to transcend their bondage
summary: Krishna explains the three energetic qualities that govern human psychology and behavior: Sattva (clarity, harmony, peace), Rajas (passion, agitation, restless craving), and Tamas (inertia, confusion, lethargy). He explains how to cultivate Sattva and ultimately transcend all three.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: tatra sattvaṁ nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam | sukha-saṅgena badhnāti jñāna-saṅgena cānagha ||
keyVerses.translation: Of these, Sattva, being pure, illuminates and is free from disease. Yet it binds, O sinless one, through attachment to happiness and knowledge.
keyVerses.context: Explains how different mental states drive our actions and emotions, providing an analytical framework for self-regulation.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Directly helps users diagnose their mental state: lethargy (Tamas), frantic hustle and burn-out (Rajas), or calm clarity (Sattva), and make mindful lifestyle adjustments.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
theme: The cosmic tree of existence, detachment from worldly entanglements, and the supreme consciousness
summary: Krishna uses the metaphor of the inverted Ashvattha tree to depict material existence whose roots lie in the transcendent. He reveals the eternal flame of awareness seated within the hearts of all living beings.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: sarvasya cāhaṁ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṁ ca | vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo vedānta-kṛd veda-vid eva cāham ||
keyVerses.translation: I am seated in the heart of all beings. From Me arise memory, knowledge, and their loss as well. By all the Vedas am I to be known; indeed I am the compiler of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
keyVerses.context: Assures the seeker that the ultimate source of intelligence, conscience, and wisdom resides within their own heart.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Provides spiritual solace to those feeling abandoned, unguided, or disconnected from their inner compass.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Divine and Demonic Natures
theme: Virtues that elevate the soul versus vices that lead to self-destruction (anger, greed, pride)
summary: Krishna delineates the qualities of the elevated mind (fearlessness, purity of heart, truthfulness, compassion, modesty) and warns against the destructive triad of desire, anger, and greed which are the gateways to inner ruin.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: tri-vidhaṁ narakasyedaṁ dvāraṁ nāśanam ātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṁ tyajet ||
keyVerses.translation: Three are the gateways to hell leading to the ruin of the self: lust/craving, anger, and greed. Therefore, one must abandon these three.
keyVerses.context: Krishna warns that unconstrained anger and compulsive craving inevitably destroy peace of mind, relationships, and moral judgment.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Essential for users struggling with intense rage, revenge impulses, jealousy, or destructive addictions.

englishTitle: The Yoga of the Three Divisions of Faith
theme: How one's innate disposition shapes faith, diet, discipline, and speech
summary: Krishna describes how faith is an inherent characteristic of consciousness, reflecting one's dominant inner nature. He defines austerity of speech (truthful, pleasing, beneficial, non-agitating) and selfless giving.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: anudvega-karaṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priya-hitaṁ ca yat | svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ caiva vāṅ-mayaṁ tapa ucyate ||
keyVerses.translation: Words that cause no distress, that are truthful, pleasing, and beneficial, alongside regular self-study—this is declared to be the austerity of speech.
keyVerses.context: Krishna teaches that truth should never be used as a blunt weapon to inflict cruelty, but communicated with empathy and beneficial intent.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Ideal counsel for family conflict, workplace communication, marital disagreements, and expressing difficult truths without causing unnecessary suffering.

englishTitle: The Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation
theme: The culmination of the Gita: nature of sacrifice, the three Gunas, the supreme secret of surrender, freedom from sorrow
summary: The concluding synthesis of all teachings. Krishna summarizes action, knowledge, agency, and intellect categorized by Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. He delivers his final intimate message to Arjuna: abandon all anxieties and fears, take refuge in truth, and arise freed from illusion.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā | vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
keyVerses.translation: Thus, I have revealed to you wisdom that is secret of all secrets. Deliberate upon this fully, and then do as you choose.
keyVerses.context: Crucial pedagogical verse: Krishna does not coerce or dictate; he enlightens, asks Arjuna to reflect deeply, and respects Arjuna's autonomous free will.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Foundational to the Krishna persona: advice is offered as illumination for the user's intellect, never as dogmatic command.

keyVerses.speaker: Krishna
keyVerses.transliteration: man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru | mām evaiṣyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo 'si me || sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja | ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
keyVerses.translation: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, and bow before Me. So doing, you will come to Me without doubt; this I promise you truthfully, for you are dearly beloved to Me. Abandon all varieties of artificial duties and simply take refuge in Me alone. I shall liberate you from all sinful reactions; do not grieve!
keyVerses.context: The Mahavakya of the Bhagavad Gita. The supreme assurance of divine love and refuge.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Ultimate comfort when a human being feels completely broken, helpless, and burdened by guilt or sorrow.

keyVerses.speaker: Arjuna
keyVerses.transliteration: naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtir labdhā tvat-prasādān mayācyuta | sthito 'smi gata-sandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṁ tava ||
keyVerses.translation: Arjuna said: 'My illusion is destroyed; I have regained my memory and inner awareness through Your grace, O Infallible One. I now stand firm, free from all doubts. I will act according to Your word.'
keyVerses.context: Arjuna's transformation from the weeping warrior on the floor of the chariot to a purposeful, lucid instrument of truth.
keyVerses.relevanceForGuidance: Demonstrates the ultimate goal of wise counsel: not dependence on the counselor, but the restoration of the seeker's own inner strength and clarity.
